quality_issues.quote: When omitted, this means no opinion and the platform is left to choose a reasonable default, which is subject to change over time.
quality_issues.suggestion: Clarify whether the current 120-second behavior is an implementation detail only or part of the expected platform contract. If it may change, document what compatibility guarantee downstream tests should enforce when the field is omitted.

quality_issues.quote: OpenShift document will suggest users to choose a wise value.
quality_issues.suggestion: Replace this with a concrete documentation or acceptance outcome, or remove it from the mitigation. If documentation is required, specify where it will live and how reviewers verify it was added.

quality_issues.quote: In practice, this window will be negligible and will not affect running pods.
quality_issues.suggestion: Add an observable verification target for this upgrade behavior, such as an e2e or upgrade check that confirms no secret mount disruption occurs while the CSIDriver object is recreated.

non_blockers: The omitted-field default semantics are explained, but the contract vs implementation-detail boundary for the 120-second default could be sharper.
The mitigation for aggressive rotation rates relies on documentation rather than a concrete acceptance deliverable.
Upgrade safety is described well, but the brief CSIDriver recreation window would benefit from an explicit verification expectation.
